strengths: Novel theoretical framework formalizing KV cache selection from output perturbation perspective; Theorem 3.3 provides principled justification for incorporating value states beyond attention weights

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple scenarios (Needle-in-a-Haystack, 16 LongBench datasets), two models, and multi-level analysis (head/layer/budget-wise) demonstrating substantial improvements in context-only compression (up to 4.41x)
Solid mathematical foundation with correct derivations and thorough appendices enabling reproducibility; extensive implementation details and prompt templates facilitate verification
Convincing empirical evidence that algorithm reduces output perturbation across >92% of heads in Llama with gains accumulating toward final layers, validating the perturbation-based perspective
Well-motivated problem formulation addressing a significant bottleneck in LLM inference; clear presentation of core ideas with proper formalization
weaknesses: Substantial theory-practice disconnect: derived upper bound θ̂ is not directly optimized; Stage 1 uses pure attention weights while Stage 2 incorporates value norms, creating unexplained asymmetry in how the theory motivates algorithm design

Limited practical improvements in realistic scenarios: only 1-2% gains in regular compression with strong Llama model (Table 1), suggesting method primarily helps when base methods already struggle; improvements are most significant in context-only compression, a less common setting

Assumption 3.4 and fixed α=0.5 lack principled justification: post-hoc validation shows 99% head satisfaction but this remains heuristic; paper acknowledges per-head adaptation could help but defers to future work, limiting algorithmic sophistication

Missing key ablations and analysis: no ablation on score combination design (why element-wise multiplication?), sensitivity to ε, computational overhead analysis, or downstream validation that minimizing L1 perturbation correlates with task performance

Limited experimental rigor: no error bars, significance tests, or variance reporting; only compares to SnapKV/AdaKV without comparison to H2O, Scissorhands, or other mentioned baselines; improvements of 1-2% could be within noise

Algorithm novelty is limited: once upper bound is derived, Algorithm 1 is a straightforward Top-K selection on combined score; the core algorithmic insight (combining attention and value norms) is relatively intuitive
Restricted model scope to two relatively small models (7-8B); limited to instruction-tuned variants of similar architecture; results on larger or diverse models would substantially strengthen claims

strengths: Novel theoretical perspective on KV cache criticality using output perturbation analysis, providing formal grounding for an intuitive problem
Mathematically sound framework with correct derivations of perturbation bounds (Theorems 3.2-3.5) and empirical validation of key assumptions (>99% in Figure 8)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across two benchmarks (Needle-in-Haystack + 16 LongBench tasks), two compression scenarios, two models, and multiple analysis dimensions (head/layer/budget-wise)
Clean practical integration into SOTA methods (SnapKV, AdaKV) without disrupting existing pipelines
Shows consistent improvements in challenging context-only compression scenario (e.g., up to 4.41x on Mistral multi-retrieval)
weaknesses: Significant theory-practice gap: sophisticated perturbation framework motivates a simple two-stage Top-K algorithm; bound looseness (from triangle inequality) is never empirically quantified; Theorem 3.5 doesn't prove optimality of the algorithm

Unjustified design choices: α=0.5 fixed across all settings without ablation; paper acknowledges this violates Assumption 3.4 for ~1% of heads but dismisses consequences without evidence; two-stage structure (pure attention in stage 1 vs. combined metric in stage 2) lacks principled justification

Modest and inconsistent improvements: regular compression shows ~0.4-0.2 point gains in Table 1 (within typical noise); some domain-task pairs show degradation with the method; no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals provided

Limited experimental scope: only compared against SnapKV and AdaKV; missing comparisons with H2O, Scissorhands, QUEST, and other recent methods; sparse attention methods discussed in appendices but not evaluated

Weak empirical support for core claims: claim that value state norms improve over attention weights alone is not convincingly demonstrated; '92% heads show lower perturbation' lacks correlation with downstream task performance; perturbation-to-quality relationship assumed rather than validated

Implementation inconsistencies and reproducibility concerns: Algorithm 1 specifies α=0.25 but text uses α=0.5; ε=1E-4 mentioned casually without theoretical justification; no code availability mentioned; missing ablation studies on key hyperparameters

strengths: Novel output perturbation perspective on critical KV cache selection, with theoretical insight that both attention weights and projected value states matter for cache criticality
Formal problem definition (Definition 3.1) and rigorous theoretical analysis with derived upper bounds (Theorems 3.2-3.5)

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple models (Llama, Mistral), compression scenarios (regular and context-only), and extensive benchmarks (Needle-in-a-Haystack + 16 LongBench datasets)

Consistent improvements over SOTA methods (SnapKV, AdaKV) with substantial gains in challenging context-only compression (up to 4.41× improvement) and 92%+ of attention heads achieving lower perturbations
Clean integration as drop-in replacement for existing cache eviction methods; detailed empirical analysis of perturbation reduction across heads, layers, and budgets
Good reproducibility: clear methodology, detailed hyperparameters, prompt templates provided in appendices
weaknesses: Significant theory-practice gap: Algorithm 1 is a heuristic two-stage greedy approach that doesn't directly minimize the upper bound θ from Theorem 3.3; Stage 1 ignores value norms despite theory emphasizing both factors

Hyperparameter α fixed at 0.5 without principled theoretical justification; empirically chosen based on power-law distribution observation; authors acknowledge head-specific tuning could improve results but defer to future work
Assumption 3.4 violated in <1% of heads (first layer), causing increased perturbation in those heads; no principled solution beyond acknowledging the limitation
Limited algorithmic novelty: two-stage greedy with combined score (A_i × ||V̄_i,:||_1) is straightforward; main contribution is theoretical rather than algorithmic
Modest empirical improvements in regular compression scenarios (e.g., 1.8%→0.9% quality loss improvement on LongBench with Llama); larger gains concentrated in context-only compression
Missing ablation studies on individual components (attention weights only vs. value norms only vs. combined); limits understanding of why value norms help and in what scenarios
Perturbation upper bound tightness not analyzed; unclear how well minimizing the bound correlates with actual perturbation reduction, potentially making optimization target less informative
Experimental rigor: no error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance testing; some improvements show marginal differences that may not be significant
